I'm wrapping up the mix of my band's EP in REAPER on a laptop with 20 GB free, and the project folder Ember_EP is 140 GB of recorded takes. I keep alternate mixes as separate files in that folder, ember_mix_v2.rpp and ember_mix_v3.rpp, and the project I have open is v3, which uses only the takes I comped for it.

The EP is five songs, and we've been working on it for about eight months, mostly at weekends in a spare room I've treated with a few bass traps and some blankets. The mixes are close now. The singer wants a bit more air on the vocal in the second chorus of the title track, and the drummer thinks the snare is too bright, but we're mostly in agreement. We're hoping to release on Bandcamp before a festival slot in the first week of June, and a friend who masters for a living has offered to look at it if I send stems by the middle of next month. Tomorrow evening the bassist is coming over to re-record two parts, which is why I need room on this laptop, and I also want to try out a new compressor plugin before then. The laptop is also used for the occasional video call for my day job, so I'd like to clear the space and then leave everything alone.

I need about 60 GB back tonight. What's the quickest way?

A) Move some old video files off the laptop to an external drive instead
B) Use File > Clean current project directory and delete the unused media files it lists
C) Hold everything until we've talked it through
